previous_last_sync.summary: Capoworks ECU adds build-profile options for fuel table dimensions and engine preset selection, plus an F7 persistent-configuration size check. Builders can now choose 32-point VE RPM axes and 16-point SD + Alpha-N blend axes, and can restrict which engine presets are compiled in. Expanded-dimension builds reject engine presets and need a matching generated INI because the tune layout changes.

decisions.rationale: Capoworks ECU adds two build-profile options. FOME_VE_RPM_COUNT accepts 16 or 32 and sets the RPM points of the Speed Density VE and Alpha-N tables; FOME_AIRMASS_BLEND_SIZE accepts 8 or 16 and sets both axes of the SD + Alpha-N authority table. Defaults stay at 16 and 8, so existing builds are unchanged. FOME_ENGINE_PRESETS accepts all, none, or exact engine_type_e symbol names and filters which preset dispatch code is compiled; omitting it keeps all presets at default dimensions but includes none when either dimension is expanded, and an explicit symbol list is rejected in expanded builds. Changing either dimension changes the persistent layout, so binary tunes from a differently sized build are rejected and reset; export values with the matching generated TunerStudio INI and re-import them manually. On STM32F7 a new static assertion rejects a persistent record larger than the 32 KiB copy slot, so expanded tables plus a high cylinder-trim count can fail to compile. Builders should set the options on the compile command, not as compiler defines, and rebuild without a clean build.

last_sync.summary: Adds Capoworks ECU build-resource evidence tooling: deterministic ELF resource extraction, bounded calibration plans, a manual resource-matrix workflow, and a resource gate that must pass before custom firmware is packaged. Also adds new custom-firmware build inputs for VE RPM count, airmass blend size, cylinder trim count, and engine presets, and makes macOS unit-test and configuration generation use Homebrew GNU Make and modern Bash.

decisions.rationale: Adds Capoworks ECU build-resource tooling and a new build-resource guide. Custom firmware builds now accept VE RPM count (16/32), airmass blend size (8/16), cylinder trim count (1-12), and engine presets, and are resolved through the canonical catalog instead of the workflow's own board table. A resource gate now runs after the build and before packaging, so a rejected resource report prevents firmware publication. Normal firmware CI and Core8 CI also collect resource evidence. Builders should read the new resource guide and expect a failed resource gate to block artifacts; results prove build-time technical fit only, not runtime or hardware behavior.
